:::{#def-expected-generalization-error}
#### Expected generalization error (expected prediction error, expected test error)

The **expected generalization error** of a [fitting procedure](#def-fitting-procedure) $\fitproc$
at training-set size $\nobs$
is the mean,
over [training sets](#def-training-set) $\trainset$ of $\nobs$ observations
drawn independently from the population,
of the [generalization error](#def-generalization-error)
of the [prediction rule](#def-prediction-rule) that $\fitproc$ produces from $\trainset$:

$$
\expgenerr{\fitproc}{\nobs} \eqdef \E{\generr_{\trainset}},
\quad
\trainset = \paren{(\Predvar_{\iobs}, \Outvar_{\iobs})}_{\iobs \in \obsidx}, \quad \abs{\obsidx} = \nobs.
$$ {#eq-expected-generalization-error}

:::

:::{#rem-source-expected-generalization-error}
#### Source: Expected generalization error (expected prediction error, expected test error)

@hastie2009elements [sec. 7.2] call this quantity the **expected prediction error**
(or **expected test error**) and write it $\generr$, without the argument $\nobs$.

:::
